The certification confirms that Geely's defined development capability - spanning functional safety, expected functional safety and AI safety - meets the requirements of three converging international standards, as intelligence becomes increasingly central to vehicle value. Geely had already established functional safety processes under ISO 26262 and SOTIF processes under ISO 21448 at concept and system level, with these processes certified by UL. Building on this foundation, Geely moved into the software phase and expanded into AI safety in line with ISO 8800:2024, developing new processes and seeking third-party certification to catch up quickly with the latest standard. Closing the gap: how we supported the certification journey We carried out a gap analysis of Geely's development processes against the requirements of ISO/PAS 8800, delivered by two experts at SGS-TÜV Saar in Germany.
